REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - MARCH 13, 2025 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at cerritos.gov and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
Order of Agenda
The City Council, by majority of those members present, may reorder the business items listed on the agenda.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at cerritos.gov, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or in writing as described below.
In-person public comment : Public comment on business agenda items will be opened and may be provided during consideration of that business agenda item. Public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and non-agenda items will be opened and may be provided during Agenda Item No. 6.
Written public comment (hard copy or email) : Public comment may be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk at 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703 no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting and retained with the official meeting record.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 or at city_clerk@cerritos.us in advance of the meeting to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

This section is reserved for public comment on Consent Calendar, Closed Session, and items not listed on the agenda but that are within the subject matter jurisdiction of the legislative body. Verbal comments will be limited to three minutes per speaker, subject to the Mayor/Chair extending to a maximum of five minutes per speaker, with a total time allotted not to exceed 45 minutes unless the Mayor/Chair extends.
7.
Consent Calendar
Items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the legislative body, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a legislative body member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

11A.
Report from City Manager/Executive Director
During this part of the meeting the City Manager/Executive Director or designated staff will have an opportunity to report on various City matters and/or respond verbally to questions or comments from the prior City Council meeting, including any request by the City Council to provide a brief supplemental report or brief follow-up response to items from the prior City Council meeting's agenda.
11B.
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports
City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Meeting Reports During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, verbal reports will also be provided in such cases where the City Council-appointed delegate and/or alternate is unable to attend a scheduled meeting, and there is insufficient time to schedule an agenda item for Council consideration of another alternate, necessitating a Mayor's urgency appointment. Requests may also be made of staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item, except to approve or ratify travel expenses for City-related business.
12.
Closed Session
12A.
CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL - EXISTING LITIGATION
Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(1) (COUNCIL)
Name of Case: Castro v. City of Cerritos (U.S. Dist. Ct., Central Dist. Cal., Case No. 2:24-cv-09625-CBM-Ex)
Closed Session Report
If the City Council adjourns to Closed Session, the City Council/Successor Agency will reconvene into Open Session after its conclusion and designated City staff will provide a verbal report on any reportable action taken. This report will be memorialized in the official meeting minutes.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE SUCCESSOR
AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY, MARCH 13, 2025,
7:00 PM, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE,
CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA.

  1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

  2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Mike Ballentine, Chaplain, Cerritos Sheriff’s Station.

  3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Councilmember Johnson.

  4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Bruce W. Barrows
  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Chuong Vo
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

  5.  Presentations/Appointments

  5A.  Presentations

  A proclamation was made by the City Council honoring:

  Mike Farrar (Red Cross Month).

  Recognition of outgoing Commission/Committee Members appointed by Mayor Solanki
  (Eric Westphal, Community Safety Committee; Daisy Mina Lagasca, Let Freedom Ring
  Committee; Leah Nass, Let Freedom Ring Committee; Pino Pathak, Parks and Recreation
  Commission; Bhavin Gandhi, Planning Commission; Latha Vasan, Property Preservation
  Commission).

  Recognition of outgoing Commission/Committee Members appointed by Mayor Pro Tem
  Vo (Habib Ali, Community Safety Committee; Mel Cortez, Community Safety Committee;
  Matthew Kauble, Fine Arts and Historical Commission; Melissa Snyder, Let Freedom Ring
  Committee; Steve Lin, Parks and Recreation Commission; Carla Gilhuys, Planning
  Commission).

  Recognition of outgoing Commission/Committee Members appointed by Councilmember
  Barrows (Martin Flax, Community Safety Committee; Patrick "Maurice" Stitt, Community
  Safety Committee; Kelly Colwell, Fine Arts and Historical Commission; Candy Yee, Let
  Freedom Ring Committee; Monica Ballentine, Let Freedom Ring Committee; David
  Albright, Parks and Recreation Commission; Gene Burd, Planning Commission).

  5B.  Informational update on the Tuesday, March 4, 2024 General Municipal Election.

  An informational update on the Tuesday, March 4, 2024 General Municipal Election was
  given by Cynthia Nava, City Clerk. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no further action on this item.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 13, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 8

  The Mayor announced the meeting rules of decorum.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period for items not listed on the meeting
  agenda but that were within the subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the
  Consent Calendar, and Closed Session.

  Gary Anderson, representative of U.S. Small Business Administration, provided
  information on assistance available for community members and small businesses who
  had been affected by the recent local wildfires. (Documents submitted to the City Council
  at a public meeting are considered public record. Public requests for copies of the full-text
  redacted written correspondence can be made during regular business hours to the Office
  of the City Clerk).

  Mark Chung, representative of the American Red Cross, thanked the City and residents
  for support and spoke regarding the agency’s efforts related to the recent local wildfires.

  Deanna Allen spoke regarding public safety in her neighborhood and requested the City
  find alternative solutions.

  Mike Ballentine thanked the City for installing the Tribute to Public Safety memorial.

  Anthony Morrow spoke regarding public safety in his neighborhood and requested the
  City continue to prioritize public safety matters.

  Harry Kim spoke regarding public safety in his neighborhood and requested the City find
  alternative solutions.

  Linda Oyoung spoke regarding public safety in her neighborhood and requested the City
  find alternative solutions.

  Bella Paiz, Diego, Angel Reyes, Adrian, and Mahi spoke regarding their school capstone
  group project, providing aide to unhoused individuals.

  Cynthia Nava, City Clerk, announced that prior to the meeting the Council/Agency
  members received full-text, unredacted copies of the one (1) written comment
  submitted for Item 5A, by the deadline listed on the agenda and for inclusion in the
  official record. Requests for copies of the written comment submitted for this meeting
  can be made during regular business hours to the Office of the City Clerk.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

7.  Consent Calendar

7A.  Approval of Minutes

7A.1. Thursday, February 27, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting
  Minutes (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to approve the Thursday,
  February 27, 2025, 7:00 p.m. City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

7B.3. Approval of Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Yokoyama, to authorize
  administrative initiated Fiscal Year 2024-25 budget amendments in accordance with Joint
  Budget Resolution No. 2024-12/CSA No. 2024-01 and the Strategic Financial Plan and
  Budget Preparation Policy (Policy 2.04) as adopted by the City Council, as follows:

  1. Account/Project: FY 2024-25 Mid-Year Budget Adjustment
  Amount:  See below
  Justification: The Mid-Year Budget Adjustment is essential for aligning the City's fiscal
  strategy with the evolving needs of the community and ensuring continued efficient
  operation of municipal services. Following a comprehensive review of all expenditures and
  revenues, adjustments have been identified to address variances from the initial budget
  assumptions. These adjustments reflect changes in revenue projections and modifications
  to expenditure accounts. This consolidated amendment is proposed to facilitate
  streamlined management and oversight, ensuring that the budget remains a dynamic tool
  that accurately reflects the City's priorities and financial reality. Details of the amendment
  have been provided in Exhibit 1 of the agenda report associated with this item. A
  summary of the adjustments is shown below:

  Summary of Revenue Adjustments
  General Fund  $(1,233,193)
  General Fund Misc.  29,870
  Special Revenue Funds  2,845,845
  Capital Project Fund  0
  Enterprise Funds  (2,566,260)
  Internal Service Fund  (5,800)
  $(929,538)

  Summary of Expenditure Adjustments
  Legislative and Administrative  $(335,020)
  Community Development  (251,843)
  Public Works  (890,203)
  Community and Cultural Services  (2,574,817)
  Community Safety  (345,322)
  Administrative Services  (267,157)
  Theater  (274,500)
  $(4,938,862)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki

7C.  Approval of a Master Joint-Use Agreement with the ABC Unified School District for use of

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Seeing none, the Mayor declared the public
  comments period closed.

7C.  (continued)

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to approve the Master Joint-Use

  with the inclusion of the following amendments:

  1. Deletion of Section 23.16, Provisions Required by Law;
  2. Deletion of the Rutan and Tucker, LLP addressee; and
  3. Replacement of the Rutan and Tucker, LLP signature line with Pam K. Lee, City Attorney

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Barrows, Johnson, Yokoyama, Vo, Solanki
  NOES:  None

8.  Public Hearings

8A.  Review and consideration to waive full reading of and introduce AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING VARIOUS CHAPTERS OF THE CERRITOS MUNICIPAL CODE,
  INCLUDING TITLES 2, 6, and 22, TO IMPLEMENT UPDATES TO THE CITY’S APPOINTED
  BOARDS, COMMISSIONS AND COMMITTEES* (COUNCIL).

  *Pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)
  Guidelines, this administrative activity is not a “project” under CEQA and is therefore
  exempt from CEQA review.

  A staff report was given by Ryan Carey, Deputy City Manager.

  The Mayor opened the public hearing and public comments period.

  Celia Spitzer suggested several modifications be made to the proposed ordinance.

  Seeing no other speakers, the Mayor declared the public comments period and public
  hearing closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Barrows, and seconded by Vo, to:

  1. Waive full reading of and introduce Ordinance No. 1049, AN ORDINANCE OF THE
  CITY OF CERRITOS AMENDING VARIOUS CHAPTERS OF THE CERRITOS
  MUNICIPAL CODE, INCLUDING TITLES 2, 6, and 22, TO IMPLEMENT UPDATES
  TO THE CITY’S APPOINTED BOARDS, COMMISSIONS AND COMMITTEES
  (COUNCIL);

  2. Amend the Boards, Commissions, and Committees Handbook to align with the
  provisions of Ordinance No. 1049; and

  3. Direct staff to prepare corresponding incorporating resolutions for future City Council
  review and consideration for the following Boards, Commissions, and Committees
  including compensation schedules, as follows:

City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 6 of 8

  Community Safety Committee  $25/month
  Disability Advisory Committee  $25/month

  Historical Committee  $25/month

  Planning Commission  $300/month, $50 monthly mileage
  Property Preservation Board  $100/month, $50 monthly mileage

9.  New and Old Business

  Prior to consideration of agenda Item 9A, Mayor Solanki recused himself from the
  discussion and consideration of this item, due to his ownership of property within one (1)
  of the neighborhoods being discussed.

9A.  Review and consideration of information related to the planned closure of Bigelow Street
  and Spinnaker Street for public safety purposes (COUNCIL).

  Pam Lee, City Attorney, clarified that, due to conflict of interest, Mayor Solanki should
  have been advised to recuse himself prior to the presentation of Item 9A from the
  February 27, 2025 City Council meeting (which was the ‘Review and consideration by the
  City Council of the potential closure of one (1) entrance into the neighborhood accessed
  by Bigelow Street and Bos Street and one (1) entrance into the Morning Sun
  neighborhood accessed by Spinnaker Street, Islandia Avenue, and Park Street for public
  safety purposes.’). Due to potential unfair hearing or due process issues under common
  law, and the presentation of additional information to the City Council at this current
  meeting, the following action from the February 27 council meeting may be reconsidered:

  As soon as feasible, temporarily close access of one (1) neighborhood entry point at
  Spinnaker Street and one (1) neighborhood entry point at Bigelow Street, for a period of
  four (4) months. This February 27, 2025 motion carried with one (1) "no" vote and one
  (1) abstention.

  The City Council expressed a desire to continue the matter to the next council meeting in
  order for staff to provide an updated staff report with the foregoing information and
  history; however, the City Council also acknowledged members of the public who desired
  to speak on this item.

  The Mayor Pro Tem opened the public comments period.

  Mel Cortez spoke regarding the cost of the neighborhood access closure, and requested
  the two (2) subject neighborhoods be considered by the City Council separately.

  Ciara Jasiewicz expressed concern regarding public safety in her neighborhood.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, March 13, 2025, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 7 of 8

9.  New and Old Business (continued)

9A.  (continued)

  Deanna Allen expressed concern regarding public safety in her neighborhood and
  requested verification of addresses of those opposing the closure of one (1) point of
  access into the subject neighborhoods.

  Elizabeth Boudreaux expressed concern regarding public safety in her neighborhood and
  expressed support for the temporary closure of one (1) point of access into the subject
  neighborhoods.

  Seeing no further speakers, the Mayor Pro Tem declared the public comments period
  closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Johnson, to direct staff to:

  1. Prepare a report for City Council consideration, at the March 27, 2025 City
  Council/Successor Agency meeting, a reconsideration of the City Council direction
  provided at the February 27, 2025 Council/Agency meeting, related to consideration of the
  potential closure of (a) one (1) entrance into the neighborhood accessed by Bigelow Street
  and Bos Street, and (b) one (1) entrance into the Morning Sun neighborhood accessed by
  Spinnaker Street, Islandia Avenue, and Park Street for public safety purposes;

  2. Bifurcate the presentation for consideration of each of the two (2) subject neighborhoods
  into individual reports; and

  3. Incorporate review by the City Attorney of the subject reports prior to the posting of the
  meeting agenda and reports (COUNCIL).

  ABSENT:  None
